grammar_rules.summary: The present conditional is formed by adding the endings of the imperfect to the future stem of the verb.
grammar_rules.explanation: For -er and -ir verbs, the future stem is the entire infinitive. For -re verbs, drop the final -e before adding the conditional endings. Irregular future stems are used as well.
restrictions: not used for factual statements in the present
exceptions: irregular future stems (e.g., être -> ser-, avoir -> aur-, faire -> fer-, aller -> ir-, etc.)
common_traps: Do not confuse with future tense; conditional endings are not future endings.

attestations.source_text: It is formed by adding the endings of the imperfect to the future stem of the verb. For -er and -ir verbs, the future stem is the entire infinitive form. For -re verbs, drop the final -e from the infinitive before adding the conditional endings.

grammar_rules.rule_name: Present conditional for wish or suggestion
grammar_rules.summary: The present conditional expresses a wish or a suggestion.
grammar_rules.explanation: Used to soften requests or express desires.

attestations.source_text: The présent du conditionnel is used to express a wish or a suggestion.

grammar_rules.summary: The present conditional makes statements or requests more polite.
grammar_rules.explanation: Used with verbs like pouvoir, vouloir, etc.

attestations.source_text: The présent du conditionnel is used to make a statement or a request more polite.

grammar_rules.rule_name: Present conditional with si clause in imparfait
grammar_rules.summary: When the main clause is in the present conditional, the si clause is in the imparfait.
grammar_rules.explanation: Expresses hypothetical situations in the present or future.
grammar_rules.formation: si + imparfait, main clause in present conditional
conditions: si clause must be in imparfait
common_traps: Do not use present conditional in the si clause.

attestations.source_text: The présent du conditionnel is used when a condition is implied. When the main clause is in the présent du conditionnel, the si clause is in the imparfait.

grammar_rules.summary: The present conditional expresses unconfirmed or alleged information, known as conditionnel journalistique.
grammar_rules.explanation: Used in press or news to indicate that information is reported but not confirmed.
common_traps: Do not confuse with factual reporting.

attestations.source_text: The présent du conditionnel is also used to express unconfirmed or alleged information. In this case it is called the conditionnel journalistique.

grammar_rules.rule_name: Savoir in present conditional equivalent to pouvoir
grammar_rules.summary: In formal French, savoir in the present conditional is the equivalent of pouvoir (can, to be able to) in the present or simple future.
grammar_rules.explanation: Used to express inability or polite refusal.
common_traps: Do not translate literally as 'would know'.

attestations.source_text: In formal French, savoir in the présent du conditionnel is the equivalent of pouvoir (can, to be able to) in the present or the simple future.

grammar_rules.summary: The past conditional is formed with the present conditional of être or avoir and the past participle of the main verb.
grammar_rules.explanation: Agreement rules of compound tenses apply.
grammar_rules.formation: present conditional of auxiliary (avoir/être) + past participle
agreement_rules: past participle agrees with subject when auxiliary is être
past participle agrees with preceding direct object when auxiliary is avoir
common_traps: Choose correct auxiliary; apply agreement rules.

attestations.source_text: The passé du conditionnel (past conditional) expresses what would have happened if another event had taken place, or if certain conditions had or had not been present. It is formed with the present conditional of être or avoir and the past participle of the main verb. The rules of agreement common to all compound tenses still apply.

grammar_rules.rule_name: Past conditional for regret or reproach
grammar_rules.summary: The past conditional expresses regret or reproach about past actions.
grammar_rules.explanation: Used to indicate what should have been done or what one would have liked.

attestations.source_text: The passé du conditionnel can express regret or reproach.

grammar_rules.rule_name: Past conditional with si clause in plus-que-parfait
grammar_rules.summary: The past conditional is usually found in sentences where the si clause is in the plus-que-parfait.
grammar_rules.explanation: Expresses hypothetical situations in the past.
grammar_rules.formation: si + plus-que-parfait, main clause in past conditional
conditions: si clause must be in plus-que-parfait
common_traps: Do not use past conditional in the si clause.

attestations.source_text: The passé du conditionnel is usually found in sentences where the si (dependent) clause is in the plus-que-parfait.

grammar_rules.rule_name: Past conditional for unconfirmed past information (journalistic)
grammar_rules.summary: The past conditional is used like the present conditional as a conditionnel journalistique to express unconfirmed past information.
common_traps: Do not confuse with factual past reporting.

attestations.source_text: The passé du conditionnel is used like the present du conditionnel as a conditionnel journalistique to express a statement not necessarily confirmed by authorities.

grammar_rules.summary: The expression au cas où (in case) is used with the present or past conditional.
grammar_rules.explanation: Expresses a possible future or past situation that triggers an action.
common_traps: Do not use subjunctive after au cas où.

attestations.source_text: The présent or passé du conditionnel are also used with the expression au cas où (in case).

exceptions_and_traps.title: Savoir in conditional not literal
exceptions_and_traps.description: In formal French, savoir in the present conditional is equivalent to pouvoir, not 'would know'.
exceptions_and_traps.correct_form: Je ne saurais vous répondre. (I cannot answer you.)
exceptions_and_traps.incorrect_form: Je ne saurais pas la réponse. (I wouldn't know the answer.)

attestations.source_text: In formal French, savoir in the présent du conditionnel is the equivalent of pouvoir (can, to be able to) in the present or the simple future.

exceptions_and_traps.title: Au cas où does not take subjunctive
exceptions_and_traps.description: Au cas où is followed by the conditional, not the subjunctive, despite its hypothetical meaning.
exceptions_and_traps.correct_form: Au cas où il pleuvrait, prends un parapluie.
exceptions_and_traps.incorrect_form: Au cas où il pleuve, prends un parapluie.

attestations.source_text: The présent or passé du conditionnel are also used with the expression au cas où (in case).

exceptions_and_traps.title: Agreement in past conditional with être
exceptions_and_traps.description: In the past conditional, past participle agrees with subject when auxiliary is être, and with preceding direct object when auxiliary is avoir.

attestations.source_text: The rules of agreement common to all compound tenses still apply.
